raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

- #47903 caches each media item's features per process, so an RL trainer rank still loads and preprocesses every item the rollout engines already processed. In the geo3k token-space recipe the trainer's media rebuild is most of `perf/data_preprocess_time`, and for video it is seconds per step.
- The cache was switched on by `--token-space-preprocess-cache-trust-url`, which conflated "the URLs name immutable media" with "cache at all".

## Modifications

- `DiskPreprocessCache(directory)`: a map from cache keys to files under one directory, shared by every process that sees it. A value is written to a temporary file and renamed into place with `os.replace`, so a reader sees all of it or none; a key whose file exists is not rewritten. Nothing is evicted: the directory lives as long as the job, like its checkpoints. Values are unpickled on read (`weights_only=False`, processor outputs carry video metadata objects), so only trusted processes may write the directory; the flag help says so.
- Cache keys drop the device index and keep the device type (video: plus whether the loader decodes on the GPU), so a trainer rank on cuda:3 hits what an engine computed on cuda:1. They also carry the transformers and sglang versions; within one job these never change a hit or a miss, they only keep a directory written by one environment from being read by another.
- Under `keep_mm_features_on_device` (cuda_ipc / cuda_vmm transport) a hit loads on the CPU while misses stay on the GPU; hits are moved to their modality's device before `torch.cat`.
- Cache `get` and `__setitem__` run in the default thread pool: a disk backend reads whole files, and the event loop and the media IO pool must not wait for it.
- New `--enable-token-space-preprocess-cache` switches the cache on: in memory within `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb`, or on disk with the new `--token-space-preprocess-cache-dir`. It requires `--enable-token-space-processor` and `--token-space-preprocess-cache-trust-url`; the in-memory form requires a positive size; the directory requires the switch. `--mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb` goes back to meaning only the memory LRU.
- Qwen3-VL on Hopper keeps cuda_ipc when the cache is on disk: only a memory budget costs the transport.

Not in this PR: the request waits for its own cache write, and concurrent misses on one key each compute and write it (2.7 writes per key measured on video items). #48304 writes behind the request and #48305 writes each key once; the TimeLens numbers below are without them.

## Tests

`test_preprocess_cache.py`: another process reads what one wrote; a written key is not rewritten. `test_mm_token_expansion.py`: the served core caches only with the switch, in memory or on disk; a hit joins the misses on their device. `test_model_overrides.py`: a disk cache beside a memory budget keeps cuda_ipc.

Run on the H200 devbox (CPU tests), each file in its own process: `test_mm_token_expansion.py`, `test_preprocess_cache.py`, `test_model_overrides.py` pass. The two failures listed in #47903 are unchanged.

End to end with radixark/miles (trainer side: radixark/miles#4651), Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct geo3k, 4 GPUs colocated, TP 1, 15 steps, means over steps 1+:

| arm | data preprocess (s) | step time (s) | train/rollout logprob abs diff | reward |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no cache (2 runs) | 0.83 / 0.86 | 93.1 / 94.3 | 0.0113 / 0.0113 | 0.311 / 0.306 |
| disk cache (3 runs) | 0.51 / 0.52 / 0.53 | 94.4 / 94.5 / 94.4 | 0.0113 / 0.0113 / 0.0114 | 0.314 / 0.314 / 0.312 |

Every trainer lookup hit (4 ranks x 1920, no misses, no writes); the engines wrote every item once per concurrent miss. A synthetic-video variant of the same recipe: data preprocess 2.31 s → 1.01 s, logprob abs diff 0.0105 vs 0.0107, step time 91.2 s → 98.3 s from the engines writing 19 MB items 2.7 times each (the write amplification above).

Qwen3.5-9B on 400 TimeLens Charades prompts (2 fps, up to 448 frames, CPU decode), 4 H200 colocated, TP 4, 16 prompts x 8 samples, 10 steps, with the miles TimeLens branch, means over steps 1+: step time 151.1 ± 15.9 s → 146.2 ± 12.6 s; the trainer's wait for its media rebuild 8.6 s → 1.0 s and its log-prob pass 38.5 s → 32.5 s (it no longer competes with the rebuild threads for the CPU); rollout 27.2 s → 28.4 s from the engines' awaited writes of 153 files (37 GB, about 240 MB per video). Every trainer lookup hit; logprob abs diff 0.0089 vs 0.0084; reward 0.43 on both. Per-step numbers and the two follow-ups' run are in #48305.

## Stack

After #47903. Main port: #48287.

+"""File-backed storage for multimodal preprocess cache values shared across processes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import errno
+import os
+import uuid
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.cache.identity import CONTENT_HASH_PREFIX
+
+
+class DiskPreprocessCache:
+    """A map from cache keys to values stored as files under one directory.
+
+    Every process that sees the directory shares it, e.g. an RL job's rollout
+    engines and trainers. A value is written to a temporary file and renamed into
+    place, so a reader sees all of it or none. Nothing is deleted: the directory
+    lives as long as the job that created it. Values are unpickled on read, since
+    processor outputs hold non-tensor objects such as video metadata, so only
+    trusted processes may write the directory.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, directory: str):
+        self.directory = Path(directory)
+
+    def get(self, key: str) -> Optional[Any]:
+        try:
+            return torch.load(self._path(key), map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
+        except OSError as error:
+            # ESTALE: on NFS, the file was removed while this read was open.
+            if error.errno in (errno.ENOENT, errno.ESTALE):
+                return None
+            raise
+
+    def __setitem__(self, key: str, value: Any) -> None:
+        path = self._path(key)
+        # A key fixes its value, so a file another request already wrote is not rewritten.
+        if path.exists():
+            return
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        # Not tempfile, which creates files 0600: other users must read them.
+        temp_path = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{uuid.uuid4().hex}.tmp")
+        with open(temp_path, "xb") as file:
+            torch.save(value, file)
+        os.replace(temp_path, path)
+
+    def _path(self, key: str) -> Path:
+        digest = key.removeprefix(CONTENT_HASH_PREFIX)
+        # Two-character subdirectories keep any one directory small.
+        return self.directory / digest[:2] / f"{digest}.pt"

+class TestDiskPreprocessCache(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_another_process_reads_what_one_wrote(self):
+        """A trainer opening serving's directory gets every field back, video metadata included."""
+        from transformers.video_utils import VideoMetadata
+
+        directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(directory.cleanup)
+        key = build_cache_key("video.mp4")
+        value = {
+            "pixel_values_videos": torch.arange(6.0).reshape(2, 3),
+            "second_per_grid_ts": [0.5],
+            "video_metadata": [VideoMetadata(total_num_frames=4, fps=2.0)],
+        }
+        DiskPreprocessCache(directory.name)[key] = value
+
+        reader = DiskPreprocessCache(directory.name)
+        loaded = reader.get(key)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(loaded["pixel_values_videos"], value["pixel_values_videos"])
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(loaded["second_per_grid_ts"], [0.5])
+        self.assertEqual(loaded["video_metadata"], value["video_metadata"])
+        self.assertIsNone(reader.get(build_cache_key("image.png")))
+        # The temporary file was renamed into place, so no partial file is left.
+        files = [path for path in Path(directory.name).rglob("*") if path.is_file()]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [path.name for path in files], [key.removeprefix("sha256:") + ".pt"]
+        )
+        # Readable by other users as the umask allows, unlike a 0600 tempfile.
+        umask = os.umask(0)
+        os.umask(umask)
+        self.assertEqual(files[0].stat().st_mode & 0o777, 0o666 & ~umask)
+        # On NFS a file removed mid-read fails with ESTALE; that is a miss too.
+        with patch(
+            "torch.load", side_effect=OSError(errno.ESTALE, "Stale file handle")
+        ):
+            self.assertIsNone(reader.get(key))
